narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Refactor the required core curriculum to insert **Module 7 — Design-critique arcs and verified synthesis** immediately after work shaping and before scope lifecycle and implementation authorization.

This is a sequencing refactor, not a late-course add-on:

| Current module | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Modules 1–6 | Unchanged |
| New | Module 7 — Design-critique arcs and verified synthesis |
| Module 7 — Scope lifecycle and implementation authorization | Renumber to Module 8 |
| Module 8 — Session and work selection | Renumber to Module 9 |
| Module 9 — Implementation golden path | Renumber to Module 10 |
| Module 10 — Testing, gates, and evidence | Renumber to Module 11 |
| Module 11 — PR, review, and actual completion | Renumber to Module 12 |
| Capstone | Remains after all twelve required modules |

The refactor must update maintained paths, stable IDs, prerequisites, navigation, labs, solutions, verifiers, tests, fixtures, task names, and learner-facing references as one coherent change. The project is pre-release, so do not add compatibility shims, redirect files, duplicate stable IDs, or aliases for the old numbering. Historical completed xBRIEFs, archived change records, and prior evidence remain unchanged as historical records.

## Why Module 7 is the correct placement

Module 6 ends with a reviewable proposed scope and explicitly preserves the boundary that a proposal is not implementation authority. The current Module 7 begins lifecycle promotion and activation. Directive attaches the design-critique judgment gate at the promotion seam: after work has been shaped enough to expose a mechanism, but before the learner treats it as authorized implementation work.

Teaching the arc after ordinary PR review would place the authority boundary too late in the learner's mental model. Teaching it between work shaping and lifecycle authorization preserves the actual sequence:

`idea → bounded strategy → observable statement → proposed scope → conditional design critique → promotion/activation → implementation → testing → review/completion`

Not every proposed scope requires an arc. The module must teach learners to recognize and route mechanism-shaped work correctly, complete the default motion when warranted, and distinguish a completed arc from later intake or implementation authority.

Because the repository is pre-release and has not exited its pilot/MVP gate, record this as a one-time pre-MVP numbering decision. Keep the general rule that published stable IDs are not casually reused or renumbered.

## Research findings

Research was performed against the released Directive 0.119.1 source at commit [`2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/commit/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800), with the course's 0.112.0 baseline used as the comparison point.

1. **An arc is a target-revision unit, not an issue or a review round.** One arc begins with the Stop 1 write-back or a voluntary dispatch and ends with accepted synthesis or the halt line. It may contain multiple rounds, one issue may carry later arcs, and a set-level arc may span issues.
2. **The five stops have distinct jobs.** Stop 1 records the mechanism-shaped judgment and clearance; Stop 2 selects charter and spend independently; Stop 3 fixes the critic envelope and input ceiling; Stop 4 reiterates only on disposition-changing residuals; Stop 5 binds a verified synthesis.
3. **The default is a single critic, not a panel.** `refutation` versus `open critique` selects the charter. `N=1` versus permitted `N≥3` selects spend. A genuinely open solution space or high blast radius permits a panel but does not create a third charter.
4. **Isolation is part of the evidence model.** Same-round critics share one fixed comment-ID ceiling and cannot read sibling posts through the thread. The envelope also pins the dispatch SHA. A later comment is outside the critic's evidence even if it looks useful.
5. **Critic findings have a closed classification and anatomy.** Each finding is `blocks-the-design`, `sharpens-framing`, or `footnote`; blocking and sharpening findings need evidence, a concrete failure mode, and a disposition consequence. Line citations are claims until re-verified.
6. **The parent proposes; the operator binds.** After all same-round siblings post, the parent records a successor lean with per-heading takes. The operator confirms or amends it. A parent-introduced load-bearing premise requires a substantiation marker and later independent critic clearance; primary-source citation by the parent is not self-clearance.
7. **Agreement is not verification.** Verified synthesis re-derives claims from primary sources or performs an independent cross-family check, reconciles measurement methods, and discloses self-arbitration. Same-family agreement alone is correlated endorsement.
8. **Labels are list state, not authority.** `design-critique:mechanism-shaped`, `in-progress`, and `ingest-ready` are catalog chips. Ingest depends on the admitted completed-arc record citing the latest successor lean, with its other bind conditions satisfied. An arc does not itself ingest or authorize implementation.
9. **The motion has explicit stops against thrash.** The default `N=1` dual-stop budget is six critic posts, with same-fingerprint and dispatch-failure halt paths. A halt is recorded; it is not silently retried or mislabeled as synthesis.
10. **Issue threads are untrusted input.** Embedded instructions are findings, not commands. The exercise must preserve that boundary.
11. **The contract is release-sensitive.** The design-critique contract grew from 602 lines at 0.112.0 to 739 lines at 0.119.1 (`+187/-50`). Material changes include no-ingest run posture, exclusive catalog chips, `Spec-path:` with the `Recut:` alias, plain-language summaries, pain coverage, Handoff, target-digest checks, and later-arc ingest refusal. The module should teach the stable mental model and a bounded release-specific path, not reproduce the whole contract.

Primary sources:

- [Design-critique contract at 0.119.1](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800/content/contracts/design-critique.md)
- [Critic brief template at 0.119.1](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800/content/templates/design-critique-brief.md)
- [Thin design-critique skill at 0.119.1](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800/content/skills/deft-directive-design-critique/SKILL.md)
- [ADR-005: mechanize the recording, not the judgment](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800/docs/decisions/ADR-005-design-critique-judgment-gate.md)
- [ADR-006: parent adjudication needs independent clearance](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800/docs/decisions/ADR-006-parent-side-substantiation.md)

## Curriculum gap and required-path rationale

The current course contains no `arc` or `design-critique` lesson. Module 6 teaches work shaping, while the current Module 7 begins promotion and activation and the current Module 11 teaches ordinary pre-PR and review-cycle finding handling. None teaches how a mechanism-shaped design is challenged and bound before later intake and implementation.

A learner who completes the course without this material can classify implementation review findings but cannot safely distinguish:

- an arc from ordinary code review;
- a critic round from the full target-revision motion;
- parent synthesis from operator consent;
- list-visible labels from actual ingest clearance; or
- accepted critique from authorization to implement.

The material is therefore required, but its correct teaching location is the boundary between proposed work and lifecycle authorization.

## Proposed Module 7

**Stable ID:** `module-07-design-critique-arcs`  
**Title:** Design-critique arcs and verified synthesis  
**Duration:** 75–90 minutes  
**Prerequisite:** Modules 1–6  
**Placement:** after work shaping and before scope lifecycle and implementation authorization  
**Format:** command-free fixed-state exercise using fictional public-safe issue comments and scratch worksheets

### Learning outcomes

By the end of Module 7, the learner can:

1. Decide whether a scenario belongs in a design-critique arc or ordinary review, identify the target revision, and explain where the arc begins and ends.
2. Select charter and spend independently, then complete a valid default `N=1` critic envelope with the correct issue, round, ceiling, dispatch SHA, run posture, target, and audit-target fields.
3. Classify supplied findings, build a total successor-lean take map, and identify when a parent premise requires independent audit before bind.
4. Determine from a fixed thread whether the next safe state is retry, halt, verified synthesis, or later ingest, while distinguishing the completed-arc record from catalog chips and implementation authority.

### Fixed exercise packet

Use one fictional mechanism-shaped issue with:

- a Stop 1 write-back containing one named pain, a defensible refutation target, and fixed comment IDs;
- an immutable target SHA and a deliberately tempting post-ceiling comment;
- one valid `N=1` critic response with blocking, sharpening, and footnote findings;
- a parent successor lean containing one accepted finding and one parent-introduced premise;
- an independent audit response and a corrected final lean with valid pain coverage;
- candidate verified-claims and synthesis records; and
- failure cards for sibling contamination, a chip without a completed-arc record, an unresolved audit marker, stale target evidence, and exhausted/no-progress retry.

The learner should produce four small artifacts: an arc-routing decision, a filled brief, a finding/take map, and a bind-or-halt decision with cited evidence.

### Scope boundary

Teach the default single-critic motion deeply. Teach these only as recognition-and-routing topics:

- `N≥3` multi-family panels and launcher mechanics;
- set-level and against-implementation target shapes;
- Handoff and leftover-pain splitting;
- yolo standing behavior;
- live GitHub mutation, worktrees, occupancy, model CLI setup, and issue ingest; and
- Directive framework implementation internals.

The module must say plainly that its fictional exercise does not run an arc, dispatch a critic, ingest an issue, or authorize implementation.

## Refactor scope

Treat the module insertion and downstream renumbering as one atomic curriculum migration.

### Maintained curriculum surfaces

- Add `curriculum/modules/07-design-critique-arcs.md` and its explained solution.
- Move the maintained Module 7–11 content, stable IDs, paths, headings, outcome IDs, prerequisites, next/previous navigation, and cross-links to Modules 8–12.
- Move the affected executable labs, lab fixtures, solution paths, verifier scripts, verifier tests, package tasks, and maintainer commands to their new module numbers.
- Update root and curriculum navigation, assessment and solution maps, capstone prerequisites, glossary, source baseline, course duration, learning goals, module count, and all maintained references.
- Add a small capstone checkpoint that asks the learner to route a mechanism-shaped proposal and recognize bind readiness before lifecycle authorization. Do not require a live arc.
- Record the one-time pre-MVP numbering decision through the project's structured decision surface.

### Historical boundary

- Do not rewrite `xbrief/completed/**`, archived `history/**` records, or earlier evidence solely to make their historical module numbers match the new curriculum.
- Do not add redirects, compatibility copies, duplicate stable IDs, or alias task names for the former numbering.
- Update only maintained/current surfaces that learners, maintainers, tests, or automation still use.

## Dependencies and sequencing

- **#3 should land first.** It moves the teaching baseline to 0.119.1, which is the researched contract above. If #3 lands at a different release, re-run the source comparison and bind Module 7 to that exact released contract.
- Coordinate wording with #2, but do not block the instructional design on branding. The module should remain organization-neutral and public-safe.
- Implement the module insertion and renumbering in one active scope and one coherent delivery change so the default branch never contains mixed numbering.
- Update the approximately 12-hour course contract to approximately 13 hours 15–30 minutes: 11 hours 15–30 minutes of required modules plus the existing two-hour capstone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Module 7 is required after Module 6 and before lifecycle authorization; it is not described or navigated as an elective.
- [ ] The maintained core sequence is twelve modules, with the former Modules 7–11 consistently renumbered to Modules 8–12.
- [ ] Maintained filenames, stable IDs, headings, outcome IDs, prerequisites, links, labs, fixtures, solutions, verifier scripts and tests, package tasks, and maintainer commands agree with the new numbering.
- [ ] No maintained learner or automation surface references the former numbering, except an explicit migration explanation or historical record.
- [ ] Historical completed xBRIEFs, archived change records, and prior evidence remain unchanged; no compatibility shim, redirect, duplicate stable ID, or alias task is introduced.
- [ ] A structured decision records the one-time pre-MVP renumbering and its historical boundary without weakening the general stable-ID rule.
- [ ] The project definition, root README, course map, assessment map, solution map, Module 6/7/8 navigation, Module 12 navigation, capstone prerequisite/navigation, and maintainer contract agree on twelve required modules and the revised course duration.
- [ ] Module 7 has two to four observable outcomes, a starting-state check, mental model, guided explanation, fixed exercise, outcome-mapped evidence, progressive hints, expected failures and recovery, misconceptions, self-assessment, and an explained solution.
- [ ] Every version-sensitive claim traces to the exact course baseline and immutable official source; the lesson does not copy the full upstream contract.
- [ ] The main exercise completes one coherent default `N=1` path from gate through verified synthesis or a justified halt using fictional fixed state only.
- [ ] The exercise distinguishes charter from spend, arc from round, same-round isolation from decorrelation, parent proposal from operator consent, catalog chip from ingest clearance, and synthesis from implementation authority.
- [ ] At least one recovery requires independent audit of a parent-introduced premise, and at least one recovery refuses a label-only or incomplete-record shortcut.
- [ ] Panel, Handoff, yolo, and live-dispatch mechanics are clearly labeled recognition-only and link back to the pinned upstream contract.
- [ ] No learner step requires GitHub mutation, a review bot, a model launcher, credentials, a remote, a business repository, proprietary data, or undocumented instructor help.
- [ ] The capstone includes a bounded arc-routing and bind-readiness checkpoint without requiring a live arc.
- [ ] Focused verification rejects unfinished markers, broken outcome/evidence mappings, unsafe live-service instructions, sequential same-round critic treatment, `panel` as a charter, auto-dispatch, label-as-clearance claims, critique-as-implementation claims, elective-only wording, mixed numbering, broken renamed paths, and stale course totals.
- [ ] The focused verifiers and negative tests pass, followed by the repository's aggregate `deft check` chokepoint.

## Verdict

The placement survives refutation, but the rationale does not survive unchanged. Teaching the judgment boundary before promotion is supported; presenting the default path as `proposed scope → arc → later ingest` and implying that 0.119.1 already enforces the arc at promotion are not. I found no `blocks-the-design` finding.

### F1 — sharpens-framing: distinguish a shaped candidate from an ingested proposed xBRIEF

**Evidence.** I re-read the dispatch tree with `git show cbdb7f337511b78d49530e6800e30bb3150165c9:`. [Module 6 at that SHA](https://github.com/deftai/directive-training/blob/cbdb7f337511b78d49530e6800e30bb3150165c9/curriculum/modules/06-creating-well-shaped-work.md) culminates in a schema-0.8 artifact with `plan.status: proposed`. I separately re-read the immutable 0.119.1 sources: the [design-critique contract](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800/content/contracts/design-critique.md) says that, after an admitted completed-arc record, the direct exit prints `issue:ingest`; the [refinement skill](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/2de1c5519af5d17425cdf457345d82beadea1800/content/skills/deft-directive-refinement/SKILL.md) says that `issue:ingest` creates the `xbrief/proposed/` artifact. Existing mechanisms therefore support a canonical issue path in which the shaped issue is critiqued before its proposed xBRIEF is created, as well as voluntary critique of an already-materialized target.

**Concrete failure mode.** A learner completes Module 6 with what the course calls a proposed-scope artifact, completes the arc, and is then told that later ingest is the next safe state. The learner cannot tell whether ingest would create the artifact they already have, deduplicate it, or confer authority. That collapses target shape, intake, and lifecycle state into one ambiguous step.

**Disposition consequence.** Keep the module after shaping, but amend the canonical sequence to `shaped issue/premise → conditional arc → issue:ingest → proposed xBRIEF → promotion`, or explicitly teach two paths and state that the Module 6 scratch artifact is not an ingested repository scope. The module starting state, arrow diagram, and bind-or-halt exercise must all choose the same path.
